column2: Where is the calculator, and how do I keep it open?
column3: The 🧮 button at the top right (or ⇧⌘Y — Ctrl+Shift+Y on a PC —, the “Shortcuts” widget, or Lists → 🛠️ Editing tools → “🧮 Calculator”) opens a small window that floats above the app: it stays open while you change screens, and even over an input window (a record, an event), so you can calculate without closing anything. Drag its title to move it, the bottom right corner to enlarge it (double-click the title: back to its place). Escape clears the box, then closes the calculator. Three tabs: 🔢 Simple (big keys, tape, memory), 🧪 Scientific, 📈 Graphs. It is not the 🧮 Spreadsheet (tables of cells to keep).

column2: How do I use the calculator with the keyboard?
column3: Type the calculation (12 × 3,5, 1/3 + 1/6, 2^10, √2…): it is redrawn neatly above (stacked fractions, powers, roots) and the result is shown in grey; Enter confirms it. A sign typed just after a result continues the calculation (“+ 8” becomes “ans + 8”). ↑ ↓ bring back earlier calculations; a click on a line of the tape takes back its result, ✎ takes back the calculation to edit it, 📋 copies it (⌘C with nothing selected copies the result). MC MR M+ M−: the memory. An error is explained in plain words under the box (“A closing bracket is missing”) and the cursor goes to the faulty spot. Fractions stay exact (1/3 + 1/6 = 1/2, the decimal value below); 200 + 10 % = 220.

column2: What can the scientific calculator do?
column3: 🧪 Scientific tab, sections above the keys (each section has examples to click): trigonometry in degrees, radians or grads (DEG RAD GRAD), hyperbolic functions, ln, log, exp, π, e, φ; complex numbers (3 + 4i, modulus, argument, conjugate, √(−4) = 2i); gcd, lcm, C(n ; k), A(n ; k), prime numbers and factors(360) = 2³ × 3² × 5, rounding; binary, octal, hexadecimal (255 in binary, 0xFF); statistics on a list [12 ; 15 ; 9] (mean, median, standard deviation, quartiles); matrices [[1 ; 2] ; [3 ; 4]] (det, inverse, product, or “▦” to write them in a grid); equations up to the 4th degree typed with “=” (x^2 − 3x + 2 = 0, with the exact value ± √…) and systems resoudre(2x + y = 3 ; x − y = 0); derivative, integral, limit, sum of a sequence. In French notation, the comma is for numbers (2,5) and “;” separates the numbers of a function: pgcd(12 ; 18). ⚙️ sets the theme, the angle, the number of digits, comma or point, fractions, the region for measures, with “💾 Saved settings”.

column2: How do I convert toises, arpents or livres-sols-deniers?
column3: In the calculator, write “3 toises en m”, “5 arpents en ha”, “12 pieds en m”, “2 toises 3 pieds en m”, “1 livre poids en g”, “785 deniers en livres” (→ 3 livres 5 sols 5 deniers), “81 livres en francs”, “100 °F en °C”, or use the “Units” section (Value, From, To). Old measures follow the region chosen in ⚙️ (Paris by default, Lyon, Brittany, Normandy, Burgundy, Provence, Lorraine, Alsace, Flanders): these are the same tables as Settings → Calendar / measures, given to 6 digits (“≈” when the value changed from one village to the next).

column2: Can the calculator count with record dates?
column3: Yes, like the date fields (C4): “3 frimaire an XII” gives 25 November 1803 and the day of the week; “14 juillet 1794 en républicain” gives 26 messidor an II; “7 mai 1925 → 8 décembre 1960” (or “du … au …”) gives the age or the gap: 35 years, 7 months and 1 day, i.e. 12,999 days. With an incomplete date (“1925 → 1960”), it gives a range. “Dates” section of scientific mode: two boxes ready to use. The French Republican calendar was only used from 22 September 1792 to 31 December 1805.

column2: How do I plot a graph?
column3: Calculator → 📈 Graphs tab: write y = sin(x), x^2/4 − 1… (up to 6 curves, each in its own colour; “＋ Add a curve”, × to remove one). Drag to move around, mouse wheel or [− 100 % +] to zoom, hover over a curve to read x and y; “⤓” downloads the image (PNG). Curves are calculated in radians. A wrong formula is explained under its line.

column2: How do I open a list or a statistic in the spreadsheet?
column3: Above a list (Lists): “⤓ Export ▾” → “🧾 Open in the spreadsheet” (the columns and filters shown) or “As CSV”. For one of My charts, a list of artists or a diagram: “⤓ Export” → “🧾 Spreadsheet”. The workbook opens without being stored: “💾 Save” keeps it in the Spreadsheet.

column2: How do I fill the spreadsheet with data from my genealogy?
column3: In the spreadsheet: Data → “⤒ Fill from the app…”. 1. What to take: 👥 People or 📅 Events (with the usual bar: 🔍 Search, Filter ▾ by sex, Sosa, place of birth, tag, years), 🏠 Censuses (a municipality, a year), 📜 Index transcriptions, 📈 Statistics (first names, occupations, ages at death…) or 📋 My lists. 2. The columns: order them with ⠿, remove them with ✕, “＋ A column taken from the data” adds one (father, mother, spouse, nationality…). 3. The preview, then “Where” (new sheet or from the chosen cell) and “⤒ Fill N rows”. People and places arrive as chips linked to their record; an empty cell in these columns is filled with the picker. “🔒 Without the living or confidential records” leaves them out (always in View-only mode).

column2: What does “Keep up to date” mean in the spreadsheet?
column3: If the “🔗 Keep up to date” box is ticked when filling, the sheet stays linked to your database: a green banner “🔗 Kept up to date” shows it, with “↻ Reload”. It is read again on its own each time the workbook is opened (and when you click ↻): new records added, deleted records removed, names and dates corrected. Columns you add on the right (a formula, a note) stay on their person’s row, even if the order changes. ⋯ → “Stop keeping up to date” keeps the values as they are. In all workbooks, a person or place chosen in a cell follows its record (new name); a deleted record becomes a grey “?” chip again.

column2: How do I turn a transcription (census, register) into records?
column3: In the spreadsheet: Data → “📤 Send to the database…” (or the button in the transcription’s banner). 1. The columns: what it creates (👤 records, 🏠 a census with its households, 📅 events) and, for each column, where it goes (Surname, First name, Age, Occupation, Relation to head…, guessed from the headings). 2. “Here is what will come in”, row by row: ALREADY IN THE DATABASE (the record is linked), NEW RECORD, TO CHECK (several possible records: choose ▾ the right one, a new record, or leave the row), PROBLEM (impossible age, missing name…: the row is left out). 3. “📤 Create N records and link N”: everything comes in at once; for a census, each household becomes a census of the municipality, the wife and children of the head are linked as a family. The message at the bottom left offers “↶ Undo”: everything just created is removed and the database is as before.

column2: How do I prepare a census transcription with the right columns?
column3: Spreadsheet → “📋 Start from a template” → “🏠 Census transcription”. The banner at the top lets you choose the year (1836 → 1936): the columns change with it (age and calculated “Born about” until 1901; year and place of birth, nationality, employer after that); rows you have already typed stay under the same heading. Choose the municipality with the place picker, type the transcription, then “📤 Send to the database…”. From Lists → 📜 Record indexes, “🧾 In the spreadsheet” opens the people and households of a page (street, no., household, surname, first name, age, occupation, relation), kept up to date; sending links each transcribed person to their record. In the Research workshop, “Add an item from the software” → “🧾 A workbook” puts a workbook (budget, schedule, table of sources) in a folder of the project, and Export → “🧾 Table of all items, in the spreadsheet” opens it right away.

column2: How do I make my family website (without knowing how to code)?
column3: Lists → 🛠️ Editing tools → “🌐 My website” → “＋ New site”: choose a template (My family, My ancestor, My village, Artist portfolio, Blank page). On the left, “＋ Blocks”: drag a header, a banner, a text, an image or a gallery (image window), and the blocks from your genealogy (tree, record, timeline, map, figures, photos of a person, people of a place) into the preview. “T Write”: click in a text to change it. “🎨 Styles”: colours, fonts, width. 🖥 💻 📱: the preview on a computer, tablet or phone. 💾 Save (⌘S) stores it in the list, with its versions.

column2: How do I link my code to the visual site (“this is my header”)?
column3: In “🌐 My website”, “◫ Both” shows the preview and the code side by side: click an element of the preview, it says what it is (“This is: header.site-entete”) and its lines light up in the code; click in the code, the element is selected in the preview. On the right, give it a role with one click (Header, Menu, Main content, Section, Footer, Card), a name, a tag, a class, an id. Typing in the code updates the preview straight away; writing in the preview updates the code. Tab expands an abbreviation: ul>li*3, div.carte>h2+p, m10 → margin: 10px;.

column2: Does my website show living people?
column3: No. The genealogy blocks (tree, record, timeline, map, figures, photos) follow the rule of “📤 Share with the family”: no living person and no confidential record, and a photo only goes out if nobody hidden is linked to it. If you have written by hand the full name of a living person, it becomes “[name removed]” in the exported site (the export window says so beforehand).

column2: How do I put my website online?
column3: In “🌐 My website”: “⤓ Export ▾” → “📦 The whole site as .zip” gives a .zip (index.html, the pages, css/, js/, images/ reduced and without GPS data, and a README). Unzip it and open index.html to see it; to put it online, send the whole folder to your web host (OVH, o2switch, Netlify, GitHub Pages…). “🌐 This page only” gives a single .html file, everything inside. “↗ Preview” opens it in a browser tab, like a visitor.

column2: Where do I put my JavaScript in My website, and is it safe?
column3: In the “Site JS” tab of the code. It only runs in “▶ Test” (an isolated preview that only sees your site, never the app or your database) and in the exported site (js/script.js). A script tag written in the HTML of a page is removed when saving, like onclick attributes and javascript: links: the message says so.

column2: How do I move a block or an element of my website?
column3: In “🌐 My website”, tool ↖ Select: take the element in the preview and drag it; a blue line shows where it will go (before, after, or inside with dotted lines when you aim at the middle of a section). With the keyboard: select it, then Alt + ↑ or Alt + ↓. The code follows on its own, and ↶ Undo puts it back.

column2: How do I put one of my diagrams on my website?
column3: In “🌐 My website”: ＋ Blocks → “🏛️ Diagram” → “One of my diagrams” (the picker) or “Create a diagram”. It is drawn by Charts → My diagrams with today’s figures, redrawn each time the site is opened, and frozen on export (the names of living people are removed). On the right: “✎ Edit the diagram”.
